what.heading: What is a list?
paragraphs: A list holds several values, in order, inside square brackets `[ ]`. You'll use lists all through this externship: the pages of an SDF, the dates you find on them, the document types you detect.

points.title: Ordered
points.text: Items stay in the order you put them in.

points.title: Counts from 0
points.text: The first item is at position 0, not 1.

example.heading: What it looks like
example.caption: `doc_types[1]` is "Certificate of Quality": the second item, because counting starts at 0.

demos.label: Get one item
demos.code:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality", "BSE/TSE Declaration"]
print(doc_types[0])

demos.label: Count the items
demos.code:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality", "BSE/TSE Declaration"]
print(len(doc_types))
demos.note: len() tells you how many items.

demos.label: Add an item
demos.code:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality"]
doc_types.append("Chain of Custody")
print(doc_types)

demos.label: Loop over it
demos.note: A for loop visits each item in order.

try.prompt: You just found a **Material Description** page. Add "Material Description" to the end of `doc_types`, then print the list.
try.starter:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality"]
# add "Material Description", then print the list
try.solution:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality"]
doc_types.append("Material Description")
print(doc_types)

checks.hint: Your list should end up with exactly 3 items. To add one item to the end of a list, use doc_types.append(...) once.
Your list has 3 items, but the last one isn't "Material Description". Check the spelling and that you added it to the end.

try.stdout_hint: Your list changed, but nothing gets printed. Add print(doc_types) on the last line.

wrong.code:
doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality"]
doc_types.append("Material Descripton")
print(doc_types)

doc_types = ["Cover Letter", "Certificate of Quality"]
doc_types.append("Material Description")
